title: Arkret Realm Read + Moderation-Policy Operation DTOs
description: Closed request/response DTOs for the self-surface Realm read operations and moderation-policy management (ak.self.realm.*). Realm read returns the lifecycle projection; export returns a full event-log + operation dump; effective moderation-policy returns the organization-inherited merged view; the moderation-policy override write carries the caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Event. See spec/v1/zh/models/realm-and-space.md and spec/v1/zh/governance/content-moderation.md.

operations.description: Operation dump rows {operation_id, realm_id, object_kind, operation_type, payload, created_at}.

events.description: Event-log dump rows {event_id, realm_id, event_kind, operation_type, operation_id, sender, payload, created_at}.

realm_effective_moderation_policy.$comment: Open extension surface: the merged moderation-policy view carries deployment-defined organization/realm policy layers and fanout metadata; additionalProperties intentionally true so servers may surface implementation-specific layer detail without a wire-breaking change.

inheritance_chain_ids.description: Organization DIDs (or deployment-local organization identifiers) contributing policy layers, parent-first.

realm_moderation_policy_event_submission.description: Caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Control Move. event.realm_id MUST equal the path Realm and event.actor_id MUST equal the authenticated session actor. The service forwards the exact submission through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT author, rebuild, co-sign or append a precondition. Admission requires ak.realm.moderation_policy or ak.policy.manage according to the capability registry; Realm ownership alone is not an authorization rule. The Event MUST contain exactly one signed head_eq precondition for ak:cell:ak.component.realm.moderation_policy.v1:null, comparing the complete settled cell value or null when absent. The payload is the closed realm_moderation_policy_state_payload and carries the policy document only as payload.value. Exact byte replay of an accepted Event returns the byte-identical stored outcome; the same event identity with different bytes, a stale head, a Bottom cell or a second applicable CAS guard fails closed without another write.

realm_moderation_policy_replace_request_.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.moderation_policy Event and no unsigned policy fields.

realm_moderation_policy_document.description: Projection of the accepted moderation-policy Event: realm_id is event.realm_id, policy is event.payload.value, updated_by is event.actor_id, and updated_at is event.created_at.

realm_lifecycle_event_submission.description: Shared submission shape for the four Realm lifecycle Moves. The Event payload MUST be carried inside the caller-signed Event; accepting it directly for a service-added signature is forbidden by capabilities.md sections 118/361 and key-management.md section 411. The Realm is single-sourced by event.realm_id and MUST equal the path realm_id. The service MUST submit these exact bytes through ordinary Event admission and MUST NOT co-sign, rebuild or synthesize the Event; admission MUST verify that event.actor_id is the authenticated caller and that the lifecycle transition is admissible from the Realm's current state. Because these payloads describe a transition out of state the caller has to read first, a concurrent lifecycle write makes the later submission fail its precondition rather than silently reordering: that is the intended outcome, not a regression.

realm_archive_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.archive Move and nothing else. The archived flag and optional reason live in lifecycle_event.event.payload (realm_archive_payload).

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.archive Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_freeze_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed ak.realm.freeze Move and nothing else. The frozen flag and optional reason live in lifecycle_event.event.payload (realm_freeze_payload).

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.freeze Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_tombstone_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.tombstone Move and nothing else. Its payload (realm_tombstone_payload) requires reason and successor_realm_id, so the signed Event is the whole record of who ended the Realm and where it continues.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.tombstone Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.

realm_destroy_request_body.description: Carries the caller-signed terminal ak.realm.destroy Move and nothing else. Its payload (realm_destroy_payload) requires reason and may pin retention_policy_id and verification_stub_required.

lifecycle_event.description: Closed ak.realm.destroy Event authored and signed by the authenticated caller.
